tagline: A capital that turns its back on a bay it could ride — Dublin Bay as the unbuilt fast lane to Howth, Dalkey and Dún Laoghaire.
summary: Ireland's marine-mobility opportunity is Dublin Bay, which strings the city's waterfront from the Docklands out to Dún Laoghaire, Howth, Dalkey and Killiney — coastal villages and headlands slow by DART and road at peak but minutes apart by sea. There is effectively no scheduled passenger water transport on the bay today. Bolt, a major ride-hail player in Dublin, can turn the bay into a fast commuter and leisure spine — a genuinely new mode for one of Europe's most congested capitals.
why_marine_mobility: Dublin's coastal suburbs and the Silicon-Docks employment core line a wide, sheltered bay that carries no commuter boats. Navier's Pioneer II flies the bay mesh — Docklands to Dún Laoghaire, the cross-bay hop to Howth, the southern run to Dalkey — turning slow rail-and-road journeys into clean minutes, while the Quanta-LR range reaches across the Irish Sea. It is a greenfield mode in a market with almost no incumbent ferry to displace.

demand_signals.label: DART coastal commuter corridor
demand_signals.note: The Howth–Bray coastal rail line runs at capacity at peak, paralleling a bay with no commuter boats — large, proven coastal travel demand with no water option.

demand_signals.label: Howth & Dalkey leisure villages
demand_signals.note: Affluent coastal villages with marinas, seafood and headland walks draw heavy weekend flows that crawl out by road and rail.

demand_signals.label: Docklands employment hub
demand_signals.note: The Silicon-Docks tech and financial cluster on the Liffey quays is a dense waterfront workplace with no water-commute option to its coastal-suburb workforce.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling commuter spine across Dublin Bay from the tech Docklands to Dún Laoghaire, Howth and Dalkey, bypassing capacity-constrained DART and congested coast roads.
Fast leisure hops to Howth and Dalkey villages and the short island runs to Ireland's Eye and Dalkey Island.
A premium cross-Irish-Sea connection on the Quanta-LR as range comes online, over a bay that today has no fast water mode at all.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The bay mesh — Docklands↔Dún Laoghaire (~6.5 nm), Howth (~7 nm), Dalkey/Killiney (~9 nm), Dún Laoghaire↔Howth (~7 nm) and short island hops to Ireland's Eye (~1 nm) and Dalkey Island (~0.3 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric range off existing harbours.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The cross-Irish-Sea trunk Dublin Port↔Holyhead (~67 nm) sits at the edge of the all-electric envelope and is the natural Quanta-LR hybrid corridor (H2 2026+), removing charging dependency on the open crossing.

signature_routes.label: Dublin Docklands ↔ Dún Laoghaire (all-electric bay commute)
Dublin City ↔ Dalkey / Killiney (southern bay run)
Dublin Port ↔ Holyhead — Irish Sea crossing (Quanta-LR)

transit_planning: For Bolt as the incumbent ride-hail brand or Dublin Port / Dún Laoghaire Harbour: a greenfield clean water tier launched via foreshore licensing and pier access, integrated with the app over a bay with no competing ferry network.
competitive_landscape: Dublin Bay has almost no on-water passenger transport to displace — only seasonal island boats and cross-Irish-Sea car-ferries from Dublin Port. The absence is the opportunity: a wide, sheltered bay ringed by affluent coastal suburbs, served only by road and rail.
regulatory_note: The bay engages Dublin Port Company, Dún Laoghaire Harbour and the Irish Maritime Administration under the Department of Transport. Much of the inner bay is a UNESCO Biosphere, favouring a zero-emission, low-wash craft. With little incumbent ferry traffic, the path is foreshore licensing and pier access rather than displacing operators.
seasonality: A temperate maritime climate gives a long but weather-variable season; summer (May–September) is the leisure peak while the commuter case runs year-round. Atlantic fronts and the exposed outer bay are the main disruption windows, where foiling's stabilised, low-wash ride extends the operable envelope.
